entry.title: I Built a Free AWS SAA-C03 Practice Tool While Studying — Here's Why
entry.summary: A few months ago I was deep in SAA-C03 prep and frustrated. Every practice tool I found was either bloated, paywalled from the start, or just multiple-choice banks with no real context. So I built my own — and then kept going until it was actually good. AWSPrepAI (https://awsprepai.netlify.app) is a focused SAA-C03 practice platform with: 533 exam-style questions across all 4 domains (Design Resilient Architectures, High Performing Architectures, Secure Applications, Cost-Optimized Architectures) A full 65-question mock exam with a 130-minute timer — same format as the real thing Visual architecture scenarios that test how well you understand AWS service interactions Keyword hints to help you think through answers, not just memorize them Zero signup required for the free tier — you just open it and start Most platforms gate everything behind a paywall. You can't even try before you buy. I wanted the opposite: let people actually use it, get value, and decide if premium is worth it. The free tier gives access to 5 questions per domain. Premium unlocks everything for $10/month, $59/year, or $99 lifetime. The hardest part wasn't the questions — it was the mock exam timer and making sure the visual architecture scenarios actually made sense without being confusing. I went through probably 6 iterations of the UI before it felt right. I also learned that building for yourself is the best way to build something people actually want. Every feature exists because I personally needed it while studying. 👉 https://awsprepai.netlify.app No account needed. Feedback welcome — especially from anyone currently studying or who recently passed the exam. Would love to know what's missing.

entry.summary:
When a production image pipeline starts producing micro-tiling, washed-out textures, or inexplicable shadows, it's rarely a single bug. As a Principal Systems Engineer responsible for an image-processing fleet during a large-scale migration in Q3 2024, the symptom set pointed to a systemic mismatch: prompt conditioning, mask generation, and post-process upscaling were each doing "the right thing" in isolation but failing together. This note peels back the layers of that failure mode, exposes the internal mechanics, and shows the trade-offs you must accept when moving from toy examples to production-grade image pipelines.
